brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.evidence: No part placed for this; 3D-printed plastic melts/ignites with a hot iron. Use a commercial metal iron stand, not a printed holder.
requirements.requirement: holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot

requirements.evidence: bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half with solder-reel prop (prop:3), visible from above
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-half-div2 with small-parts prop (prop:4) showing spare-tips storage; cold tips only

finish.summary: Built a 2-cell bench caddy with a half-depth bin for solder and a divided half-depth bin for cold spare tips. No holder for a hot powered iron was built: it would be unsafe in 3D-printed plastic. Park the hot iron only in a commercial metal stand.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your hot-iron holder can't be printed plastic — I'll build the safe solder-and-tips storage instead.
